title: Extension of embeddings and intrinsic weights
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\Fq$, and
$k=\Fbar$, the fixed algebraic
closure of $k_0$. Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
choose an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\mathbf Q$, and
set

$$
\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}=
\{z\in\Qlb:z\text{ is algebraic over }\mathbf Q\}.
$$

An ell-adic realization is an isomorphism
$\jmath:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}$;
this is the algebraic-closure
notion, with the finite-field datum.
Fix $i\in\mathbf Z$, a number field
$L\subset\Qlb$, and a field embedding $\sigma:L\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$.
There is an abstract field isomorphism

$$
\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C
$$

whose restriction to $L$ is $\sigma$. If $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$
is such that

$$
|\iota(\jmath(\alpha))|=q^{i/2}
$$

for every ell-adic realization $\jmath$ and every abstract field isomorphism
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, then

$$
|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}
$$

for every $\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$.
The $q$-Weil-number condition of weight $i$
is stable under
$\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$.

proof.text: View $\Qlb$ as an $L$-extension through the given inclusion, and view $\mathbf C$ as an $L$-extension through $\sigma$. The latter is legitimate because a field embedding is injective. A finite $\mathbf Q$-basis of the number field $L$ gives a bijection of its underlying set with $\mathbf Q^n$ for a finite $n$; this is countable. Thus $L$ is countable for both extension structures. This uses only the finite-dimensional definition of a number field and finite rational coordinates, and needs no separate lemma.

source.place: ## Proof, first paragraph, countable coefficient fields; direct-base variant using L instead of its relative algebraic closure.

proof.text: The field $\Qlb$ is algebraically closed by its assumed algebraic-closure structure, and $\mathbf C$ is algebraically closed by [lem-weil-complex-algebraically-closed]. The cardinality of the canonical algebraic closure $\Omega_\ell=\operatorname{PadicAlgCl}(\ell)$ is $2^{\aleph_0}$ by [lem-weil-padic-algebraic-closure-cardinality]. Both $\Omega_\ell$ and the chosen $\Qlb$ are algebraic closures of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, so [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique] gives a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-isomorphism between them. As a bijection it transfers this cardinality to $\Qlb$. By [lem-weil-complex-cardinality] the other ambient field has the same cardinality. Since $2^{\aleph_0}>\aleph_0$ by Cantor, both ambient fields are uncountable.

source.place: ## Proof, first paragraph: both ambient fields have cardinality continuum; algebraic-closure uniqueness is Stacks 09GV, lemma-algebraic-closures-isomorphic.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-transcendence-basis-exists] to the two $L$-extension structures from step 1. Obtain bases $(b_s)_{s\in B_\ell}$ in $\Qlb$ and $(c_t)_{t\in B_{\mathbf C}}$ in $\mathbf C$. Apply [lem-weil-countable-base-transcendence-cardinality] to each: its base is the countable field $L$, each ambient field is algebraically closed and uncountable by step 2, and these are transcendence bases. Hence $|B_\ell|=2^{\aleph_0}=|B_{\mathbf C}|$, and choose a bijection $e:B_\ell\to B_{\mathbf C}$.

source.place: ## Proof, first paragraph: choose transcendence bases and match their cardinalities; existence is Stacks 030F, lemma-transcendence-degree.

proof.text: Put $A=L[b_s:s\in B_\ell]\subset\Qlb$ and $A^{\prime}=\sigma(L)[c_t:t\in B_{\mathbf C}]\subset\mathbf C$. Algebraic independence identifies these polynomial subalgebras with polynomial rings over the abstract coefficient field $L$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]. Explicitly the coefficient $a$ evaluates to $a$ in $A$ and to $\sigma(a)$ in $A^{\prime}$. Renaming $X_s$ to $X_{e(s)}$ therefore defines a ring isomorphism $f:A\to A^{\prime}$ with $f(a)=\sigma(a)$ and $f(b_s)=c_{e(s)}$. The inverse renames using $e^{-1}$ and applies $\sigma^{-1}$ on $\sigma(L)$; the two composites fix every coefficient and every variable, hence every polynomial. Both subalgebras are domains, since they lie in fields. Define $\widetilde f:\operatorname{Frac}(A)\to\operatorname{Frac}(A^{\prime})$ by $a/b\mapsto f(a)/f(b)$. It is well-defined because $a/b=a^{\prime}/b^{\prime}$ means $ab^{\prime}=a^{\prime}b$, an equality preserved by $f$; its inverse is the same formula with $f^{-1}$. Thus $\widetilde f$ is a field isomorphism extending $\sigma$. These are explicit substitutions and fraction identities, rather than a new lemma.

source.place: ## Proof, first paragraph: the bijection of bases and coefficient isomorphism define an isomorphism of rational function fields; Stacks 030E, definition-transcendence (1)-(2).

proof.text: By [lem-exc-transcendence-basis-algebraic-closure], $\Qlb$ is an algebraic closure of $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $\mathbf C$ is an algebraic closure of $K^{\prime}=\operatorname{Frac}(A^{\prime})$. Regard $\mathbf C$ as a $K$-extension through $K\xrightarrow{\widetilde f}K^{\prime}\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$. Its algebraic closedness is unchanged; every polynomial relation over $K^{\prime}$ pulls back coefficientwise through $\widetilde f^{-1}$ to a nonzero relation over $K$, so it remains algebraic over $K$. Now both ambient fields are algebraic closures of the same field $K$. Apply [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique] to these two specified structure maps. It gives $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ with $\iota(x)=\widetilde f(x)$ for $x\in K$. For $a\in L\subset K$ this reads $\iota(a)=\sigma(a)$, proving the prescribed-restriction clause. Notice that an unspecified abstract isomorphism between the ambient fields would not suffice.

source.place: ## Proof, first paragraph: extend the rational function field isomorphism to the algebraic closures; Stacks 09GV, lemma-algebraic-closures-isomorphic.

proof.text: Choose an $\ell$-adic realization $\jmath$ using [lem-weil-realization-exists], so the universal hypothesis on realizations is not vacuous. Fix any $\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$. Since $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ is algebraic over $\mathbf Q$, [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] applied to the single generator $\alpha$ shows that $\mathbf Q(\alpha)$ is a finite extension of $\mathbf Q$. Its image $L_\tau=\jmath(\mathbf Q(\alpha))\subset\Qlb$ is isomorphic over $\mathbf Q$ to it and is therefore a number field (the images of a finite basis form a finite basis). The restriction of $\jmath$ to $\mathbf Q(\alpha)$ is bijective onto this image. Define $\sigma_\tau:L_\tau\to\mathbf C$ by $\sigma_\tau(z)=\tau((\jmath|_{\mathbf Q(\alpha)})^{-1}(z))$. This composite is a field embedding. Apply the extension constructed in steps 1-5 with $L_\tau,\sigma_\tau$. The resulting isomorphism $\iota_\tau$ satisfies $\iota_\tau(\jmath(\alpha))=\tau(\alpha)$. The assumed equality for this $\jmath$ and this $\iota_\tau$ gives $|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$, as required.

source.place: ## Proof, second paragraph: transport any embedding of Q(alpha) using a realization, and apply the first clause. Finiteness of a simple algebraic extension is Stacks 09GH, lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated.

proof.text: For the last clause take any nonzero $q$-Weil number $\beta\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of weight $i$ in the sense of [def-weil-numbers], and let $\gamma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$. The automorphism fixes the rationals and sends $\mathbf Q(\beta)$ isomorphically onto $\mathbf Q(\gamma(\beta))$, since each generated field is the smallest subfield containing its indicated generator [def-weil-simple-field-extension]; apply the same inclusion argument to $\gamma^{-1}$ for equality. Given an embedding $\tau^{\prime}:\mathbf Q(\gamma(\beta))\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$, its composite with this restriction of $\gamma$ is an embedding of $\mathbf Q(\beta)$. Hence $|\tau^{\prime}(\gamma(\beta))|=|(\tau^{\prime}\circ\gamma)(\beta)|=q^{i/2}$. Also $\gamma(\beta)\ne0$ by injectivity. This proves the Weil condition for $\gamma(\beta)$ directly from that for $\beta$, independently of the stronger realization hypothesis. Applying this to $\gamma^{-1}$ also gives equivalence of the conditions.

source.place: ## Proof, third paragraph: Galois stability by composing embeddings.
